conservation.condition_narrative: Dust particles were removed. Re-framed in consultation with the O’Keeffe Foundation and the National Gallery of Art (Judy Walsh and Hugh Phibbs). The frame is a recreation of a George Off profile 291 that was used at the NGA for Stieglitz frames. Hugh Phibbs made the spacers for the frame. The spacers are wood wrapped with paper and the side visible is painted to match the putty-colored frame.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by the National Portrait Gallery (Washington, D.C.) in 2025. This report contains information from reports done both March 18, 2002 and January 18, 2022.
conservation.technical_description: The copper frame was designed by Georgia O'Keeffe. It was framed with glass, no spacer, and a particle board backing. There were screws into the side of the frame securing it to the particle board. Some pastel had offset onto to the underside of the glass. The pastel was determined to be very friable. The drawing board had possibly been cut down from a larger size due to the roughly cut edges at the right and bottom. There is a flattened wrinkle on the surface of the drawing paper at the bottom center, edge. There is some delamination of the lower right corner of the drawing board. Along the top edge is evidence of pastel abrasion. Some test strokes of pastel are located at the bottom right side of the paper surface.

credit_line: The Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation, Abiquiu, New Mexico, 1993
description: Depicts Beauford Delaney, an American modernist painter.  In this composition, his face is seen in profile and facing to the left, looks downward with a neutral expression. Delaney wears a white collar. His head and neck occupy the center of the composition, surrounded by a slightly shaded background and large expanses of exposed gray cardboard.
